title: Dynamic shape-aware adapter and prefill throttling framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a shape-aware kernel adapter and a conservative prefill throttling framework that uses a lightweight ML predictor + heuristic guardrails to choose between FlashAttention v2, FlashAttention v3, and the stable generic kernel during prefill and decode. Motivation: we observed intermittent regressions when v3 is selected for certain short/batched workloads (higher jitter and tail latency) despite improved median throughput on long contexts. This ticket scopes the adapter, predictor training and evaluation, telemetry schema, rollout shims, and an automated rollback hook that triggers on SLO regressions. Key ideas: 1) fingerprint input shape and runtime signals (seq_len distribution, batch_size, head_count, d_model, quantization, GPU arch, free workspace) and compute an expected cost/latency delta for each kernel; 2) run a compact ML model (decision tree / light GBM) in the hot path to rank kernels; 3) combine ML rank with safety thresholds: if expected p99 increase > 5ms or predicted success probability < 0.85, prefer fallback kernel; 4) apply prefill throttling when kernel-switch churn or warmup penalties are detected (limit rate of v3-samples per-worker, maintain warmup budget); 5) telemetry: emit selection_reason, predicted_delta_ms, model_confidence, firing_guardrail, warmup_state, and buffer_handoff_events.
acceptance_criteria: Shape-adapter implementation integrated into runtime kernel selection hook and enabled behind feature flag
ML predictor serialized and loaded at runtime (<200KB on-disk) with <=2ms infer cost on GPU host CPU per request
Canary rollout plan documented and implementable via console routes with circuit-breaker thresholds
Automated telemetry dashboards showing selection distribution, p50/p95/p99 latency by kernel and shape bucket
Fallback and rollback triggers that revert to stable kernel automatically when p99 latency exceeds baseline by >10% for 5m
rollout_plan: Dev-only: feature-flag run on staging with synthetic load (Jan 25 - Jan 31)
Canary: 2% of production requests, cross-GPU types, monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate (Feb 07 - Feb 14)
Ramp: 10% -> 25% after stable metrics for 2h each; stop/rerollback if guardrail triggers
Full: enable for selected model families after 72h of stable telemetry and manual sign-off
experiment_results_summary: On internal benchmark suite (mix of short chat prompts and long-context LLM generation): ML-driven adapter preferred v3 for long-contexts (>1024) and v2 or generic for short contexts. Results vs baseline (always-v2): median latency -3.2% overall, p99 latency -11.8% on long-context tests, but p99 +6.1% regressions on one short-chat bucket when no warmup budget enforced. With prefill throttling enabled (20% warmup budget per worker), short-chat p99 regressions disappear and overall token-cost reduced by ~4.7% on average. Predictor inference cost ~1.4ms on an m5-large-like host, model size 42KB (serialized tree).
